summary: Add customer_note column, initialise from note, deploy new version with state-only migration, create a PostgreSQL trigger that keeps note and customer_note in sync, retire old version, then drop note column.
write_consistency: A database trigger fires after every INSERT or UPDATE on account_user, copying the value from note to customer_note and vice‑versa, ensuring both columns always hold the same note regardless of which version wrote it.
revision_notes: Plan a4 failed because interleaved writes left note and customer_note diverging; adding a trigger guarantees synchronous values across versions.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and copy existing note values.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

stages.description: Ensure all rows have matching values in both columns.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL OR customer_note != note;

stages.description: Create a trigger that keeps note and customer_note in sync for all subsequent writes.
Retire the old version so it no longer serves traffic.
Drop the note column after the old version is retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
